newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Foreign buying propels Singapore shares higher.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying propels Singapore shares higher.

text.p: A fresh injection of foreign funds, notably from the U.S., boosted the Singapore stock market to a firmer close on Thursday, dealers said.
"The Singapore market is benefitting from a renewed flow of funds into this region as evident by the generally firmer regional bourses like Indonesia (and) Thailand," a dealer said.
After a flat open, the key Straits Times Industrials Index rebounded to an intraday high of 2,105.82 before ending at 2,102.73, up 22.28 points or 1.07 percent.
Market turnover was moderately active, at 105.1 million, with gainers swamping losers 217 to 98.
"We are also seeing syndicates back in the picture, punting in Labroy Marine and Indonesian-linked stocks like United Pulp & Paper," the dealer said.
Labroy Marine, which ended up S$0.01 at S$1.24 (US$0.88), topped the actives with 5.8 million shares.
Singapore Press Foreign led gainers, rising S$0.40 to S$24.60, while Creative Technology fell S$0.15 to S$8.90.
Dealers said investors awaited U.S. October book-to-ratio data, due shortly, for a clearer direction to the electronic sector. The SES electronic index was up 0.14 points at 81.34.
